Synopsis:
The player can talk to Marhyah or Dringo to mention they found Scratch. Depending on who the player spoke to first, either Dringo or Mat'hyah will be the initial speaker.In either case, Mar'hyah will dominate the conversation.Mar'hyah wants to reclaim him as property of the couriers' office. The player can convince her to release Scratch, and potentially even to leave the kennels altogether. If they fail to persuade her, Scracth is locked up, and Oyster Boy can get fired.

Cluster Contexts:
- WYR_Posthouse_EquerryGroom.json: This takes place at Withers’ epilogue gathering near the kennels where Scratch — the owlbear the party raised — has been found by the player. Mar'hyah is the hard‑edged courier‑office kennelmaster who treats her staff (like the young attendant Dringo) brusquely and insists the courier animals are office property. Which NPC speaks first depends on who you approached, but Mar'hyah dominates the exchange and will try to reclaim Scratch unless the player persuades her to release him — possibly even to let Scratch leave the kennels. If persuasion fails, Mar'hyah will lock Scratch up and Dringo risks punishment or losing his job; other companions are nearby but off‑screen, making this a social, post‑conflict scene.
- CAMP_Courier_Dog.json: In SwA, Scratch speaks like a human. He doesn't have any kind of dog-like affectation, nor is he stupid - he's well-spoken, even when he's saying 'dog' things.Scratch, the dog a dead courier we met during our travels, appears in our camp at night, having retrieved something. We can engage in a little tug of war in order to see what he's fetched.
- FOR_Courier_Dog.json: In SwA, Scratch speaks like a human. He doesn't have any kind of dog-like affectation, nor is he stupid - he's well-spoken, even when he's saying 'dog' things. Throughout the dialogue, he's stoic but heartbroken, deluding himself into believing that his master is not dead.We come across the corpse of a man being protected by his loyal dog, Scratch.The dog refuses to let us near the dead man or his belongings, forcing us to try and win him over (or else just kill him). We can use Speak with Animals to get further insight into the dog's perspective.
 If we cast Speak with Dead upon the courier, we can learn the dog's name and use this as an additional way to win it over.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_CourierDog.json: Courier dog's dialog during the goblin hunt celebration party. The camp will be full of either tieflings or goblins. If the tieflings are present, Scratch is excited and playful; if the goblins are present, he's scared and anxious.
- CAMP_OwlbearCub_CFM_Dog.json: The player hears an uproar in the camp and  think the owlbear’s turned on Scratch. When they investigate, they discover the cub is having a nightmare and the dog is comforting him. The player can talk to them and confirm that there's no danger. Subsequently, the cub will be a permanent feature in the camp, with new behaviours with Scratch, plus a new default dialogue.Note: if the player decides to not investigate the sounds, the animals will be moved off-stage for the remainder of the night/the sounds will stop, The player won't know what happened until they see the animals again. If they have SwA, they can learn that there was nothing wrong.

context: This scene takes place at Withers’ epilogue gathering near the courier kennels after the player discovered Scratch — the owlbear the party raised — and brought the news to the staff. Mar'hyah is the hard‑edged courier‑office kennelmaster who treats her young attendant Dringo (the “Oyster Boy”) brusquely and insists the courier animals are office property. Which NPC opens the exchange depends on who the player spoke to first, but Mar'hyah dominates the conversation and will try to reclaim Scratch as office property. The player can persuade her to release Scratch — possibly even allow him to leave the kennels — but if persuasion fails Scratch will be locked up and Dringo may be punished or lose his job; other companions are nearby off‑screen.
